content.title: How UnitedHealth will be getting 'back to basics' in 2026
content.description:
UnitedHealth Group (UNH) is among the five stocks that have been dragging the Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI) lower in 2025, dropping by 33% year-to-date.

This month also marks one year since UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson was killed in New York City in December 2024.

Columbia University health policy professor Meghan Fitzgerald explains her view on public sentiment toward UnitedHealth and the American healthcare industry.

Fitzgerald is also Grey Ghost Capital's private equity investor, a board member of Tenet Healthcare, and a former nurse.

content.title: Affordable Care Act: Lawmakers should target healthcare red tape
content.description:
As Republican lawmakers begin to align with House Democrats on extending Affordable Care Act (better known as Obamacare) subsidies, what is the general consensus among Americans on healthcare affordability?

These ACA tax credits — which work to lower the cost of health insurance and reduce recipients' monthly premiums — are set to expire on December 31.

Columbia University health policy professor Meghan Fitzgerald outlines how sharply healthcare costs and insurance fees will rise if these subsidies expire and why lawmakers should prioritize cutting down on waste and red tape for Americans to receive proper treatments.

Fitzgerald is also Grey Ghost Capital's private equity investor, a board member of Tenet Healthcare, and a former nurse.

content.summary: From novel pharmaceuticals to telemedicine, most healthcare companies are on a mission to drive better patient outcomes. Players catalyzing medical advancements have benefited from elevated demand, which has supported the industry’s returns lately - over the past six months, healthcare stocks have gained 14.1%, nearly mirrorring the S&P 500.

content.title: 1 Value Stock to Consider Right Now and 2 We Find Risky
content.summary: Value stocks typically trade at discounts to the broader market, offering patient investors the opportunity to buy businesses when they’re out of favor. The key risk, however, is that these stocks are usually cheap for a reason – five cents for a piece of fruit may seem like a great deal until you find out it’s rotten.
